core_obligations: Unwind the hypothesis: for a prime q in the associated primes of M over S there is an element m of M whose annihilator in S is exactly q (proof lines 15553-15554).
Compute the annihilator of that same element m over R and find that it is the contraction q intersected with R, which exhibits the contraction of q as an associated prime over R (proof line 15555).
proof_roadmap: Use the annihilator description of associated primes to produce a witness element m for a prime q over S (proof lines 15552-15554).
Read the R-annihilator of m as the contraction of the S-annihilator and conclude the inclusion of sets (proof lines 15555-15556).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring map from R to S and an S-module M, the image under the induced map on spectra of the associated primes of M over S consists of associated primes of M over R (statement lines 15545-15550). The proof does not pass through primary decomposition or localisation: it unwinds membership in the associated primes to an element whose annihilator is the given prime, and then observes that the same element has the contraction of that prime as its annihilator over R (proof lines 15552-15556). The content is the identification of the two annihilators of one and the same element, and the author writes it out in full. H2.
